rich_summary: After the fall of Ravana’s forces, Hanuman returns to Rama with Sita’s message: she longs to see her lord again after the long torment of captivity. Moved by the news, Rama—overcome with emotion—orders Vibhishana to bring Sita before him, bathed and adorned with celestial perfumes and jewels. Though Sita wishes to see her husband immediately without bathing, she ultimately obeys Rama’s command out of devotion. She is prepared and carried in a palanquin under Vibhishana’s escort. When Rama learns she has arrived, conflicting emotions surge within him—joy, anger, and grief from her long stay in the enemy’s palace. Concealing his happiness, he asks that she be brought closer, foreshadowing the difficult test he is about to impose. The chapter marks the tense prelude to the famous trial of Sita’s purity.

highlight_spans.why: A moral reflection on compassion—even toward wrongdoers—setting the ethical tone that frames the characters’ conduct.
Hanuman’s promise that Sita will soon behold Rama again—a pivotal turning point from captivity toward reunion.
Rama’s command to bring Sita adorned with celestial ornaments formally initiates their long‑awaited meeting.
The line describing how rage, joy, and grief overwhelm Rama captures the emotional complexity of the reunion.

top_scenes.scene_text: Hanuman kneels before the sorrowful Sita in the Ashoka grove, promising that she will soon see Rama shining like the full moon among his allies.
Sita, adorned with radiant jewels and garments, rises into a palanquin carried by titans under Vibhishana’s command as she is escorted to meet Rama.
Rama stands among warriors on the battlefield’s edge as Sita’s palanquin approaches, his face torn between joy, grief, and restrained anger.
